deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the fair copy (p.3, 'Riemann 3', Nachlass folio 17r) of the 1859 Monatsberichte paper 'Ueber die Anzahl der Primzahlen unter einer gegebenen Grösse'. The page continues from the previous page's integral representation Π(s/2-1)π^{-s/2}ζ(s) = 1/(s(s-1)) + ∫_1^∞ ψ(x)(x^{s/2-1}+x^{-(1+s)/2})dx, with ψ(x)=Σ_{n≥1} e^{-n²πx}, and the definition ξ(t)=Π(s/2)(s-1)π^{-s/2}ζ(s), s=1/2+it. In modern notation Π(z)=Γ(z+1), so ξ(t)=Ξ(t)=½s(s-1)π^{-s/2}Γ(s/2)ζ(s).

(1) Formula for ξ. [My filled step] Π(s/2)=(s/2)Π(s/2-1), so ξ(t) = ½s(s-1)·[1/(s(s-1)) + ∫...] = ½ + ½s(s-1)∫_1^∞ψ(x)(x^{s/2-1}+x^{-(1+s)/2})dx. With s=½+it one has s(s-1) = -(t²+¼). Also x^{s/2-1}+x^{-(1+s)/2} = x^{-3/4}(x^{it/2}+x^{-it/2}) = 2x^{-3/4}cos(½t log x). Hence ξ(t) = ½ - (t²+¼)∫_1^∞ ψ(x)x^{-3/4}cos(½t log x)dx.

(2) Second form. ξ(t) = 4∫_1^∞ (d/dx)[x^{3/2}ψ'(x)]·x^{-1/4}cos(½t log x)dx. [My filled step] Integrate by parts twice, using (d/dx)(x^{-1/4}cos(½t log x)) and its derivative. The boundary terms at x=1 cancel the constant ½ because of 4ψ'(1)+ψ(1) = -½. That identity follows by differentiating 2ψ(x)+1 = x^{-1/2}(2ψ(1/x)+1) at x=1.

(3) Analytic properties. ξ is entire in t (finite for all finite t). It is even, since the functional equation gives s↔1-s, i.e. t↔-t. Its Taylor series in t² converges very fast, because ψ(x) decays like e^{-πx}.

(4) Location of zeros. For Re s>1, log ζ(s) = -Σ_p log(1-p^{-s}) is finite, so ζ(s)≠0 there. The other factors Π(s/2), (s-1), π^{-s/2} are also nonzero there. By the symmetry t↔-t (s↔1-s) the same holds for Re s<0. Hence zeros satisfy |Im t| ≤ ½, i.e. 0 ≤ Re s ≤ 1.

(5) Zero counting. The number of zeros with 0 < Re t < T is ≈ (T/2π)log(T/2π) - T/2π. Argument: (1/2πi)∮ d log ξ(t) around the rectangle -½ ≤ Im t ≤ ½, 0 ≤ Re t ≤ T counts the zeros. Riemann asserts the integral equals (T log(T/2π) - T)i up to an error of order 1/T. [Modern: the Stirling main term from the Γ-factor, i.e. θ(T)/π+1.]

(6) The conjectures. Riemann says one finds about that many real roots in this range. He calls it 'sehr wahrscheinlich' that all roots are real (the Riemann Hypothesis). He set aside a proof after a few fleeting attempts, since it was not needed for his immediate purpose.

(7) Product formula. log ξ(t) = Σ_α log(1 - t²/α²) + log ξ(0), where α ranges over the roots; correctly, one root of each ±α pair. Justification: the density of roots near t grows only like (1/2π)log(t/2π), so the sum converges and grows at most like t log t. The difference from log ξ(t) is then an even function of t, finite for finite t, and o(t²) at infinity. Hence it is a constant, fixed by setting t=0.

(8) Setup for the prime-counting formula. F(x) is the number of primes < x, normalized at jumps by the midpoint value. This prepares the explicit formula on the next page.
errors: Zero-counting error term: Riemann claims the contour integral equals (T log(T/2π) - T)i up to an error of order 1/T. This is not correct as stated. The true count is N(T) = (T/2π)log(T/2π) - T/2π + 7/8 + S(T) + O(1/T), with S(T) = O(log T) and not small. The O(1/T) claim holds only for the smooth Γ-factor (θ(T)) part. This is a known criticism (von Mangoldt, Edwards).

Zero-free region: the argument gives only |Im t| ≤ ½ (0 ≤ Re s ≤ 1, closed strip). That no zeros lie on Re s = 1 was proved only in 1896 (Hadamard, de la Vallée Poussin). Riemann's 'zwischen ½i und -½i' is fine only if read as a closed strip.

Product formula: the justification that the difference is constant is heuristic. It needs a growth bound on log ξ(t) (an entire function of order 1), first supplied by Hadamard (1893). The asserted growth 'unendlich wie t log t' was likewise not proved.
Ambiguity in the indexing of α: if α runs over all roots, the factors (1 - t²/α²) double-count each ±α pair. The sum must be over roots with positive real part (a known ambiguity noted by Edwards).

The density-of-roots claim (roots near t have density ~ (1/2π)log(t/2π)) depends on the unproved counting formula. Riemann's statement that about that many roots are real was later partly justified by Hardy (1914), Selberg (1942) and Levinson (1974).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of the fair-copy manuscript of Riemann's famous 1859 paper, with text essentially identical to the published version. All content is well known and credited to Riemann.

checkable.asserts: The kernel x^{s/2-1}+x^{-(1+s)/2} equals 2x^{-3/4}cos(½t log x) (should simplify to 0)
The first integral formula at t=0 reproduces ξ(0) ≈ 0.4971
4ψ'(1)+ψ(1) = -1/2, the identity needed for the second (integrated-by-parts) form of ξ
The Riemann–von Mangoldt main term ≈ 29 matches the 29 zeta zeros with 0<Im s<100
The first root α≈14.1347 of ξ(t)=0 is real in t (ζ vanishes on the critical line), consistent with the RH remark

transcription_corrections: Second ξ formula: the exponent of x is written in a small hand near the x and reads like x^{1/4}, with the minus sign faint or missing. The mathematically correct and published reading is x^{-1/4}; keep '[?]' or note this.
Line 1: the image shows 'tt' with an ink blot ('tt* + 1/4'); the intended reading is (tt + ¼).
Logarithms are written 'lg' (lg x, lg ζ(s), lg T/2π) in the manuscript; the transcription normalizes them to log.
'Diese Function ist für alle endlichen Werthe von t [-...-] endlich': there is a struck-through fragment before 'end-' at the line end, which the transcription correctly marks as deleted.
Before 'denn da die Dichtigkeit' there is a struck-through 'Denn', which the transcription correctly records as [-Denn-].
